title: A Synopsis - The Swiss Family Robinson

topics.name: Same word as noun and verb (hold, return, mark, value)

options: Jenny returns to England was a happy event.
Jenny's return to England was a happy event.
Jenny returned to England was a happy event.
questions.rule: The subject of was must be a noun phrase. Here return is a noun: Jenny's return.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: When the family woke up, the other passengers had leave the ship.
When the family woke up, the other passengers have left the ship.
When the family woke up, the other passengers had left the ship.
questions.rule: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: had + past participle = had left.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive voice = be + past participle: were filled.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After let me, use the base form of the verb: Let me hold.
Past perfect = had + past participle: had passed.

questions.after: a cave, Fritz shouted with joy.
questions.rule: The -ing participle shows what Fritz did: Finding a cave, he shouted with joy.
Passive: subject + was + past participle (caught).

chat: What did Father say about the gourds?
options: He said that they will made excellent bowls.
He said that they would make excellent bowls.
He said that they would makes excellent bowls.
questions.rule: In reported speech will becomes would, and would is followed by the base verb make.

options: A rubber tree was found by Fritz.
A rubber tree is found by Fritz.
A rubber tree was find by Fritz.
questions.rule: Simple past active becomes was/were + past participle: was found by Fritz.

options: Jenny said that I was happy there.
Jenny said that she were happy there.
Jenny said that she was happy there.
questions.rule: I becomes she, am becomes was and here becomes there.

options: Elizabeth told to William that she wanted a safer home.
Elizabeth told William that she wanted a safer home.
Elizabeth said William that she wanted a safer home.
questions.rule: Tell takes a person directly: told William. Said needs to: said to William.

options: A ladder was made from rope and bamboo.
A ladder was make from rope and bamboo.
A ladder were made from rope and bamboo.
questions.rule: Singular a ladder takes was, and the passive needs the past participle made.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had lived.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After the family's we need a noun. The noun form of arrive is arrival.
With by the whole family the sentence is passive: was + past participle = was carved.
A reported yes/no question is joined with if or whether, not that.
The participle phrase Thinking ahead describes the subject, Father, who comes right after the comma.

options: No, it has already left when I reached the stop.
No, it had already leave when I reached the stop.
No, it had already left when I reached the stop.
questions.rule: The bus left before I reached, so use the past perfect: had already left.

chat: Can you tie the rope to the post?
options: Yes, I will a knot it tightly.
Yes, I will knot it tightly.
Yes, I will knotted it tightly.
questions.rule: Here knot is a verb, so it follows will in the base form, with no article: I will knot it.

questions.source: Father said to Jack, "Climb the pole carefully."
options: Father told Jack to climb the pole carefully.
Father told Jack that climb the pole carefully.
Father told Jack to climbed the pole carefully.
questions.rule: A command is reported with told + person + to + base verb: told Jack to climb.

options: Rowing hard, the family reached the shore.
Rowed hard, the family reached the shore.
Rowing hard, the family reaching the shore.
questions.rule: Use the -ing participle for an action done by the subject, and the main clause needs a finite verb: reached.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The past perfect (had been) is paired with a simple past action: when Fritz found her.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive = were + past participle: were destroyed by a herd of elephants.
Asked is past, so will shifts to would, and a modal takes the base verb with no to: would support.
After the adjective great we need a noun: great value. Here value is a noun.
In a reported question the word order is like a statement: what the message meant, not 'what did the message mean'.

chat: What did the captain ask you?
options: He asked where had we come from.
He asked that where we had come from.
He asked where we had come from.
questions.rule: A reported wh-question keeps statement order (we had come) and does not use that.

chat: Who wrote The Swiss Family Robinson?
options: It was wrote by Johann David Wyss.
It written by Johann David Wyss.
It was written by Johann David Wyss.
questions.rule: Passive = was + past participle. The participle of write is written.

questions.prompt: Combine the sentences using a participle.
questions.source: Father saw the footprints. He knew elephants had come.
options: Seeing the footprints, Father knew elephants had come.
Saw the footprints, Father knew elephants had come.
Seen the footprints, Father knew elephants had come.
questions.rule: The first action becomes an -ing participle phrase: Seeing the footprints, Father knew ...

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Past perfect needs had cleaned. Singular a feast takes was prepared.

options: The captain asked Fritz where did he live.
The captain asked Fritz where he lived.
The captain asked to Fritz where he lived.
questions.rule: Reported questions use statement order (where he lived), and asked takes the person directly.

options: The journals were handed over to the captain.
The journals was handed over to the captain.
The journals were hand over to the captain.
questions.rule: Plural journals takes were, and the passive needs the past participle handed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a quick we need a singular noun: a quick return. Here return is a noun.

questions.before: No sooner had the ship left
questions.rule: No sooner had ... than is a fixed pair. The past perfect shows the first action.
Passive with a modal: can + be + past participle = can be made.

chat: Why were you so tired yesterday?
options: Because I have walked five kilometres in the sun.
Because I had walk five kilometres in the sun.
Because I had walked five kilometres in the sun.
questions.rule: The walk happened before you were tired (past), so use the past perfect: had walked.

chat: What did the doctor tell you?
options: She told me not to eat street food for a week.
She told me to not eating street food for a week.
She told me don't eat street food for a week.
questions.rule: A negative command is reported with told + person + not to + base verb.

questions.source: The ladder was built by the boys.
options: The boys were built the ladder.
questions.rule: was built is simple past passive, so the active is simple past: The boys built the ladder.

questions.source: Fritz said to Jenny, "Do you want to go to England?"
options: Fritz asked Jenny did she want to go to England.
Fritz asked Jenny if she wanted to go to England.
Fritz asked Jenny if you wanted to go to England.
questions.rule: A yes/no question is reported with asked ... if; you becomes she and want becomes wanted.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: The story is past, so the boys had grown. Fritz is one person, so Fritz was.

options: Father told Fritz that the bird might have came from far away.
Father told Fritz that the bird might have come from far away.
Father told to Fritz that the bird might have come from far away.
questions.rule: Might have takes the past participle come, and told takes the person without to.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With along with, the verb agrees with the first subject, the captain: was amazed.

questions.before: Jenny's father believed that his daughter
questions.rule: After a past verb (believed), an earlier past action takes the past perfect: had survived.
Reported statement: told + person + that + clause with the past tense wished.

chat: What did Jenny say when she saw the ship?
options: She said that she had never be so happy.
She said that she had never been so happy.
She said that she had never been so happier.
questions.rule: Past perfect = had + been. After so use the plain adjective happy.

questions.source: The captain will publish Father's journals.
options: Father's journals will published by the captain.
Father's journals will be publish by the captain.
Father's journals will be published by the captain.
questions.rule: Future passive = will be + past participle: will be published.

questions.source: Elizabeth said, "I want to stay here forever."
options: Elizabeth said that she wanted to stay there forever.
Elizabeth said that I wanted to stay there forever.
Elizabeth said that she want to stay there forever.
questions.rule: I becomes she, want becomes wanted and here becomes there.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Past reporting verb said; the participle phrase Looking at describes William; the main verb is past: agreed.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: which refers to the singular lamp, so was rescued. Passive needs the participle: was hung.

questions.rule: Past perfect = had lived. Use told + person: told the captain that ... (said needs to).
